rubric_definition: After you make the edit that one reviewer is asking for, does the other reviewer's comment still stand? If it is discharged too, the two findings are one defect; if it survives, they are different defects that share a location. If a reviewer offers two alternative fixes, either one discharging the other comment makes it one defect. Contradictory prescriptions to the same lines are different defects, because no single edit satisfies both.
evidence: Both findings report that the new module-scoped `routeVimHistoryToStore` monkey-patch of `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo` is untested, and both ask for a vim-keymap test that presses `u`/`<C-r>` (or calls the commands directly) and asserts `store.undo()/redo()` is reached — a single added test discharges both comments.

panel.finding_key: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts::new vim history routing (`routevimhistorytostore`) has no test at all
panel.summary: New vim history routing (`routeVimHistoryToStore`) has no test at all
panel.evidence: editor.ts:28-60 adds a global monkey-patch of `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo` so vim's `u` / `<C-r>` reach `store.undo()/redo()`, including a read-only fall-through branch (`cm.cm6.state.facet(EditorView.editable)`). Grepping the whole notes package for `vim`/`CodeMirror.commands` shows the only vim test is `editor.test.ts:156 'switches the keybinding mode (default <-> vim)'`, which only asserts `api.getKeymap()` and text preservation — it never presses `u`, never invokes `CodeMirror.commands.undo`, and never checks the store's history moved. So the whole routing function, its facet lookup, its editable guard and its `defaultVimHistory` fall-through can break silently. Since CodeMirror's own history is now disabled, a regression here means vim users lose undo entirely with a green suite.

coderabbit.evidence: **Add vim-mode coverage for `routeVimHistoryToStore`.** This block tests default-keymap history bindings (Mod-z / Mod-Shift-z). No test in the diff exercises `editor.ts`'s `routeVimHistoryToStore`, which routes vim's `u` / `<C-r>` to the store by monkey-patching `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo`. This is new, module-scoped routing logic; a regression there would go undetected. Add a test that switches the editor to `vim` keymap and dispatches `u` / `<C-r>` (or calls `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo` directly against the mounted view's `CodeMirror` instance) to confirm it reaches `store.undo()` / `store.redo()`.
